subject: Multi-cloud offer catalog segmentation & regional packaging — alignment request
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aws-partners.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: gcp-listings@partnergcp.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + marketplace packaging alignment (quick sync)

Hi Nikhil / Redwood team,

Thanks for agreeing to carve out time on short notice. AWS partner GTM is coordinating listings and co-sell enablement across AWS, GCP, and Azure for Acme Analytics' upcoming deployment. Before we lock offers into each cloud's catalog, we'd like to align on a couple of cross-cloud constraints so co-sell motion and quoting remain consistent.

High-level ask:
- Confirm tier definitions (what goes in "Base / Core", "Business / Enterprise", "Dedicated/Private") and associated SKU boundaries.
- Call out regions that must be blocked or require a private-package (EU data residency, APAC latency pockets).
- Packaging differences we should expose per cloud (metered units vs seat-based, dedicated capacity SKUs).

I've attached a 1-pager agenda and dropped an initial offer-catalog spreadsheet link in case you want to update live: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-redwood-offer-catalog [attachment: agenda.pdf (1 page PDF)].

Proposed quick outcomes for the sync: shared SKU mapping for AWS/GCP/Azure, one canonical pricing banding approach for quoting, and a mutual action plan for co-sell enablement.

Can you confirm if Redwood has a single canonical set of SKUs you prefer we list per cloud, or if you want separate cloud-native SKUs (recommended for marketplace compliance but harder for co-sell quoting)?

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Torres
Partner Programs — AWS Marketplace
elena.torres@aws-partners.com

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aws-partners.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, gcp-listings@partnergcp.com
Date: 2027-04-04T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + marketplace packaging alignment (quick sync)

Elena — thanks for the note and the agenda. Quick response with our starting position so the sync can be efficient.

Proposal (Redwood default):
1) Offer segmentation:
   - Core (hosted API): metered per-token + light support; public SKUs in all clouds.
   - Enterprise (reserved/dedicated capacity): monthly committed capacity SKU; explicit quota unit mapping across clouds.
   - Private (on-prem/VPC): "Private Deployment" SKU — separate listing where required for compliance (EU/DE, APAC regulated).

2) Region rules:
   - US: full catalog across AWS/GCP/Azure.
   - EU: require "Private Deployment" packaging for customers requesting customer-managed VPC or when KMS/HSM key control is demanded (list EU countries: DE, FR, NL).
   - APAC: prefer dedicated capacity SKU in selective regions (SG, JP) due to latency and support windows.

3) Co-sell / quoting: keep canonical internal SKU ids (RedwoodOffer-CORE | -ENT | -PRIV) and publish cloud-specific listing IDs. This lets sales quote consistently while marketplaces maintain their listing IDs.

Notes/asks for today:
- Kimberly, can you call out legal/compliance constraints for EU packaging?
- Karthik / Logan, we'll need a one-sheet for co-sell enablement that maps internal SKUs -> cloud listing IDs + minimum commitment buckets. I made a starter tab in the sheet Elena linked.

If that looks right, we can lock these as the default and produce a MAP (mutual action plan) for Acme.

Thanks — Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Marketplace GTM — Redwood Inference
[attachment: packaging-guidelines-v1.docx (draft)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aws-partners.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + marketplace packaging alignment (quick sync)

Adding compliance lens—quick bullets:
- EU data residency: For customers who require customer-controlled keys or data residency guarantees, we must route them to the Private SKU. Listing text should clearly state what is and isn't included in the public hosted offer (e.g., no customer KMS).
- Contracts: Marketplace transactable subscriptions must surface our standard DPA addendum; for Private offerings we need a separate procurement flow (PO + SOW).
- Tax/locale: In a few EU countries (e.g., DE), we must allow a resale/legal entity mapping in the listing metadata; this will affect how we map billing entities per cloud.

Practical recommendation: keep three canonical internal SKUs but create cloud-native listing variants that append region tags and a compliance flag, e.g., Redwood-ENT-aws-us, Redwood-ENT-aws-eu-priv. That makes automation easier for quotation tools and still keeps a single source of truth.

I'll drop a redline in the packaging-guidelines doc with the specific language we should require in listing copy.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Contracts & Compliance — Redwood Inference

From: Rajiv Mehta <rajiv@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@aws-partners.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: gcp-listings@partnergcp.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-05T15:42:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Intro + marketplace packaging alignment (quick sync)

Thanks everyone — this framing is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from Acme's side:
- Pricing bands: our procurement team prefers simple tiers for initial POC (Core) vs. Production (Enterprise). Can you provide recommended min/typical/max pricing buckets for each SKU so we can model TCO in our RFP?
- Co-sell triggers: we want a one-page MAP that calls out the exact moment we hand to AWS/GCP field for co-sell (sign-of-interest > $X ARR or technical readiness checkpoint).

I've attached a draft MAP that outlines our expected timeline and decision gates: [attachment: MAP-Acme-Redwood.xlsx (MAP, 3 tabs)].

Happy to jump on a 30-min working session this week to finalize the mapping.

—Rajiv
Rajiv Mehta
Head of Cloud Platforms — Acme Analytics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro + marketplace packaging alignment (quick sync)

Agree with the proposed approach. Action items I'm committing to before the working session:
- Karthik: produce a pricing band recommendation spreadsheet (min/typical/max) for CORE/ENT/PRIV mapped to token and seat equivalents (sheet: Pricing-Bands v1).
- Logan: create the co-sell enablement one-pager that lists the co-sell trigger thresholds and the field handoff steps.
- Kimberly: finalize the listing copy requirements for EU private flag and DPA callouts.
- Nikhil: finalize canonical internal SKU IDs and create the "listings" tab in the shared sheet for AWS/GCP/Azure listing IDs.

I'll schedule a 30-min session for 2027-04-08 (proposed times in the spreadsheet). If that works, I'll add a calendar invite and include a short agenda.

Thanks all — Karthik
